issues.title: PowerShell -v/-i flags silently consumed by b4w.ps1 parameter binder

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -- snapshot -v 0 --stdout
./b4w.ps1 snapshot -v 0 --stdout
./b4w.ps1 "snapshot" "-v" "0" "--stdout"
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The snapshot command should execute with -v 0 flag, showing viewport 0 of the accessibility tree.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The -v flag is consumed by PowerShell's parameter binder (matching -Verbose). The CLI receives 'snapshot 0' or 'snapshot-0' as the command, producing 'Unknown command: snapshot-0' or help text. Even quoting each argument individually does not prevent the issue when running via bash → pwsh -File.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: When bash invokes ./b4w.ps1 (shebang: #!/usr/bin/env pwsh), pwsh receives arguments via -File mode. Despite b4w.ps1's param() block using ValueFromRemainingArguments, pwsh's own parameter binder processes -v and -i before the script's param() runs. The b4w.ps1 script's $SafeArgs quoting (lines 442-447) runs inside the script, which is too late — the flags are already consumed. The SKILL.md documents this but the workaround (-- separator) fails with pwsh -File. The b4w.sh wrapper solves this by using -Command mode with individually-quoted args.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1: line 16-19 (param block), lines 442-460 (SafeArgs construction). The fix likely requires changes to how the script receives or forwards arguments, potentially using --% (stop-parsing) or $args instead of param().
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Document that b4w.ps1 should ONLY be used from within a pwsh terminal, not from bash
- Update b4w.ps1 to detect when -v/-i are being consumed and emit a clear error: 'Flag -v was intercepted by PowerShell. Use b4w.sh from bash, or run snapshot -v 0 from within pwsh.'
- Consider rewriting b4w.ps1 param() to not use ValueFromRemainingArguments and instead use $args directly
- Make the -- passthrough work reliably from bash: the script should strip -- but preserve all subsequent args as literals
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Amazon bot detection blocks browser4-cli — captcha loop on homepage

sections.body: ./b4w.sh goto "https://www.amazon.com" — the page shows 'Click the button below to continue shopping' captcha challenge. Clicking 'Continue shopping' redirects to /errors/validateCaptcha.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Amazon homepage should load normally, showing product categories and search bar.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Amazon's bot detection identifies the automated Chrome instance and presents a captcha challenge. Direct navigation to product pages intermittently works but is unreliable. The session degrades over time, eventually showing 'Sorry! Something went wrong!' (503 error).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Amazon uses sophisticated bot detection (likely checking for automation flags, missing WebGL fingerprint, headless Chrome markers, etc.). Browser4's Chrome instance is detected as automated. The direct-search-URL workaround (goto 'https://www.amazon.com/s?k=...') bypasses the homepage captcha but product detail pages still trigger detection occasionally.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Document common anti-bot challenges and workarounds for major sites (Amazon, Google, etc.)
- Provide a 'stealth mode' or user-agent/profile configuration to reduce bot detection
- Add support for loading browser profiles with existing cookies/sessions to bypass detection
- Document the 'prefer direct search URLs over homepage navigation' pattern as a workaround
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: go-back to search results changes element refs, requires re-snapshot

sections.body: Click a product from search results, then go-back to results, then try to click another product using previously noted refs.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The page is the same search results page — refs should ideally be consistent or the user should be warned.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Refs change after go-back (though sometimes they happen to match). The user must re-snapshot and re-discover refs, adding friction to the comparison shopping workflow.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: go-back triggers a page load which re-renders the DOM, generating new backend node IDs. This is inherent to CDP behavior, but the UX could be smoother.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Consider a 'snapshot cache' that remembers ref-to-element mapping across go-back/forward when the page content hasn't changed
- After go-back, automatically capture a snapshot and diff against the previous snapshot of the same URL to surface ref changes
- Add a 'compare N products' workflow: 'browser4-cli compare e1 e2 e3' that visits each product and produces a comparison table
